chunks: Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Salih ibn Abi al-Aswad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Masjid al-Sahla was mentioned, so he said: 'Indeed, it is the residence of our Master (Imam al-Mahdi) when he arrives with his family.'

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.صَاحِبُنَا: Our Master, a title referring to Imam al-Mahdi (peace be upon him)
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ السَّهْلَةِ: Masjid al-Sahla (The Mosque of the Plain), a specific location in Kufa associated with the Imam's return

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Masjid al-Sahla in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) identifies Masjid al-Sahla in Mecca as the specific dwelling place of Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.) upon his return, accompanied by his family. This tradition underscores the sanctity of this location in Shia eschatology, linking the physical geography of the Haram to the establishment of global justice. It reflects the scholarly view that the Mahdi's arrival will be marked by a restoration of true worship and governance rooted in the Prophet's legacy.
